scope.description: Whole Tesseract engine and tooling breadth across useful recognition and maintenance families.
scope.denominator: Image and page recognition, layout and segmentation choices, languages and models, structured document outputs, configuration and vocabulary, orientation and script detection, and model training and evaluation.

coverage.rationale: A single English-model page recognition path provides useful text and word boxes, but most language, layout, output-format, configuration and training capabilities remain outside the integration. The estimate concerns the whole application rather than recognition accuracy on its small qualification corpus.

scope.description: Bounded one-page OCR into explicitly unreviewed text, word boxes and native confidence, with captured image/model inputs and optional declared origin bound to pixels.
scope.denominator: User intent and domain decisions within this one-page machine-draft workflow; excluded languages, layouts, outputs and training are outside this denominator.

abstraction.rationale: A recognition operation produces an inspectable review trail and hides subprocess configuration and TSV parsing. Authors still supply a pinned model file, choose a native-derived segmentation mode and compose document rendering or later correction themselves; the interface does not decide whether recognised words are correct.

limitations: One opaque RGB8 non-interlaced PNG and one explicitly pinned LSTM model, exposed as English; the model's language content is not established by its filename or hash. The interface has two segmentation modes and bounded image/model sizes; no general PDF, multipage, layout, handwriting, correction or training workflow.

Native confidence is uncalibrated, output is a machine draft, and pixel consistency does not certify text truth or human review. Native availability and source-bound qualification remain separate readiness facts.
Subjective source-contract assessment rounded to five points; no exhaustive API denominator or recognition-accuracy measurement supports these percentages.
